results.title: North Macedonia: Kriva Palanka seeks help over 1,000 free-roaming cows
results.content: More than 1,000 cows are roaming freely through Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia, damaging property and alarming residents. The mayor wants the government to declare a 30-day state of crisis.

results.title: Turkey: Six-metre Trojan Horse spills plastic waste at COP31
results.content: A giant Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste has appeared in Antalya as Greenpeace International staged a striking environmental protest during the COP31 climate summit. Created with Danish artist Thomas Dambo, the Greenpeace installation warns of the environmental impact of plastics.

results.title: Burundi: 11 opposition parties announce support for President Ndayishimiye's re-election bid
results.content: Burundi’s President Evariste Ndayishimiye has secured the backing of 11 opposition parties when he runs for re-election next year.

results.title: Kenyans brace for El Niño rains as flood survivors fear a repeat of 2024 devastation
results.content: The warning comes as Nairobi continues to grapple with urban planning challenges, encroachment on wetlands and construction in flood-prone areas, factors that increase the city's vulnerability to flooding.

results.title: New witness due in former South African minister's corruption trial
results.content: Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula faces 12 counts of corruption and one of money laundering, stemming from her time as defence minister.

results.title: Swiss hospital discharges Ebola patient after successful treatment
results.content: A Swiss woman who contracted the strain of Ebola linked to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been discharged from hospital in Geneva, health officials said on Thursday.

results.title: Iran showcases missiles as military targets US army radar in Bahrain
results.content: The Revolutionary Guards said on Friday that it had destroyed a US early-warning radar in the Gulf country, the first such claim in months.

results.title: Ukraine: Russian drone attacks hit Kyiv hospital, leave two dead in Odesa
results.content: Russian overnight attacks on Ukraine killed at least two person in Odesa and injured another at a hospital in Kyiv. Rescuers evacuated patients, including people using wheelchairs and crutches, as firefighters battled the flames.

results.title: South African town divided over plan to fence in baboons
results.content: Now, a plan to move around 60 animals into fenced enclosures has split the community. Some residents say enough is enough. Others say the baboons should remain free.

results.title: UN security council extends Central African Republic peacekeeping mission until 2027
results.content: The latest mandate extension underscores the Security Council's continued commitment to the country, while highlighting the importance of a carefully managed transition that ensures national institutions can sustain the gains made.

results.title: Outlook outage hits users in 74 countries as Microsoft seeks fix
results.content: Microsoft said on Thursday that efforts to repair a major outage of Outlook were not going as expected and the firm was seeking alternative solutions as users around the world were left without its crucial services.

results.title: Portugal: Humanoid robots take centre stage at Web Summit 2026
results.content: Dancing humanoid robots and robotic dogs stole the show at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon. The technology conference has generated nearly €2.5 billion for Portugal's economy over the past decade, according to a study.

results.title: Peru: Pope Leo XIV leads youth prayer vigil at Lima's National Stadium
results.content: Thousands of young Catholics gathered at Peru's National Stadium in Lima on Thursday 12 November for a prayer vigil led by Pope Leo XIV, transforming the venue into a sea of lights, The stands lit up with thousands of mobile phone lights as the pontiff led an evening of songs, prayer and reflection.

results.title: Jensen Huang quits Nvidia as scandal rocks AI giant
results.content: Jensen Huang, the leather-jacketed architect of the artificial intelligence boom, resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.

results.title: COP31 activists urge leaders to act on climate crisis
results.content: Speaking at a news conference on the sidelines of the talks, Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg warned that the world is heading towards more genocides, ecocides and the loss of basic rights.

results.title: UN food agency chief calls for end to Sudan war as famine crisis deepens
results.content: The UN says around 34 million people — nearly two-thirds of Sudan’s population — need humanitarian assistance. It has also warned that drone attacks by both sides have killed civilians, including children, and disrupted essential services.

results.title: US: New Congress members pose for traditional photo at Capitol
results.content: Newly elected US lawmakers gathered on Capitol Hill on Thursday 12 November for a traditional group photograph ahead of the opening of the 120th Congress. The incoming House members are attending orientation following the November midterm elections.

results.title: Five candidates confirmed for Gambia's presidential election
results.content: The Gambia’s electoral commission has confirmed five candidates for next month’s presidential election. They include incumbent Adama Barrow who is running for a third term despite initially promising not to do so. It’s not clear whether more candidates are still to be named.

results.title: Cairo Film Festival opens as Middle East war weighs on cinema
results.content: The 47th Cairo International Film Festival got underway on Wednesday in the Egyptian capital. The event brings together filmmakers, actors and other prominent figures from around the world. This year’s festival is taking place under the shadow of the Middle East war.

results.title: Peter Obi supporters and journalists attacked at campaign event in Nigeria
results.content: Violence broke out in Lagos on Thursday as members of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress gathered for a town hall meeting. Participants were forced to flee as suspected protesters armed with sticks, machetes and axes tried to force themselves into the event.

results.title: Ghana announces first-ever hydrocarbon discovery in carbonate reserve
results.content: Ghana's President John Dramani Mahama on Wednesday announced the country's first-ever hydrocarbon discovery in an offshore carbonate reserve. The well lies some 150 kilometers off Ghana's coast in water more than 2000 meters deep.

results.title: War in Ukraine: Putin Meets with envoys from the U.S. President
results.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned European leaders on Thursday against discussions between the United States and Russia

results.title: Gaza: Devastation inside Nasser Hospital after deadly Israeli strike
results.content: An Israeli airstrike hit Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early on Thursday 12 November, killing six people, including a doctor, and injuring at least 27 others, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

results.title: South Africa's ANC backs Ramaphosa despite local election losses
results.content: Days after a drubbing at the ballot box, the leaders of South Africa's ruling African National Congress met to discuss the way forward. In last week's local elections, the party's vote share dropped by 15 points to just 31 percent.

results.title: UN weighs peacekeeping cuts in Central African Republic as mandate expires
results.content: The UN Security Council is set to decide on the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate, which expires this weekend.

results.title: Russia: Soldier killed in car explosion in Saint Petersburg
results.content: A Russian serviceman was killed when his car exploded in Saint Petersburg on Thursday. Investigators have opened a murder inquiry, while local media report that another person was injured.

results.title: Mississippi elects first Black US Senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction
results.content: The US state of Mississippi has made history - electing its first Black Senator in 150 years and its first Democratic Senator since 1982. Forty-three-year-old Scott Colom narrowly beat incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith marking a seismic shift for the conservative southern state.

results.title: Ukraine: Russian drone attack sparks major fire in Kyiv residential building
results.content: A Russian drone strike sparked a major fire at an apartment building in Kyiv, Ukraine, early on Thursday. Residents fled to safety as firefighters battled the flames and rescue workers helped people at the scene.

results.title: Ghana unveils new cedi banknotes celebrating national heritage
results.content: Ghana has unveiled a new series of banknotes featuring prominent historical figures and national landmarks, as the country moves to modernise its currency and strengthen protection against counterfeiting.

results.title: Trial of more than 1,200 people accused of illegal gold mining opens in Conakry
results.content: The trial of more than 1,200 people charged with illegal gold mining opened in Conakry on Wednesday amid a recent crackdown on the practice.
